corpora.name: human-mc4-wide
corpora.what: Every paragraph an automatic filter pulled from 11 mC4 shards: webshop pages (cart, stock or price words), a product noun such as mok, poster, tas, hoesje or deken plus shop vocabulary, 25 to 220 words, at most 2 per domain. Not checked by hand, so it also holds some travel copy, B2B copy and a little machine translation. One more paragraph was in the set but cannot be rebuilt from a single mC4 line, so it was removed.
corpora.source: mC4 Dutch, validation shards 0-3 and train shards 17, 123, 256, 389, 512, 640 and 777, https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/c4
corpora.license: mC4 is released under ODC-BY 1.0 and the Common Crawl terms of use. The paragraphs belong to the sites, so only URL, crawl date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: human-mc4-reviewed
corpora.what: Product and shop-copy paragraphs from Dutch-language webshops (.nl 208, .be 31, other 30), each read by hand. Reviews, blogs, news, spam and machine translation were removed (103 of 372 candidates). A subset of human-mc4-wide.

corpora.name: human-mc4-heldout
corpora.what: The same automatic filter on three further shards, keeping only domains that are not in human-mc4-wide. Built after the first list was frozen; two patterns were dropped and one narrowed after looking at it, so it is no longer fully independent.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web
corpora.what: 2,000 random pages of the Dutch web: the prose paragraphs of each page (12 or more words, enough function words, few capitals; scripts/lib/prose.mjs), 40 to 1,200 words, spam keywords excluded, drawn by a seeded shuffle (seed 42) by scripts/sample-mc4-web.mjs. URLs already in the Dutch product corpora excluded. A check against ordinary prose of every kind.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: human-mc4-web-holdout
corpora.what: 1,000 further pages from the same shuffle, kept back while the general candidates were chosen.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: human-mc4-news
corpora.what: 599 pages from Dutch and Flemish news sites (nos.nl, nu.nl, ad.nl, volkskrant.nl, hln.be, standaard.be, regional broadcasters and others), every qualifying page in the shard that was not already in another Dutch corpus. Same prose filter as human-mc4-web. News stands in for edited general prose.
corpora.license: ODC-BY 1.0 for mC4, plus Common Crawl terms; the page text belongs to each site, so only URL, date, shard and SHA-256 are shipped.

corpora.name: ai-imitation
corpora.what: Dutch descriptions for mugs, t-shirts, posters, blankets, tote bags, stickers, phone cases and a few other gift items, generated with Claude in the default style of chat assistants. About 20 are deliberately plain.
corpora.caveats: Written with the candidate patterns in view, so hit rates here are optimistic.

corpora.name: ai-gpt4-ultrachat
corpora.what: The first assistant reply of the 8 conversations in UltraChat 200k Dutch whose user asked for a product description and got one (gpt-4-1106-preview). Found with the dataset viewer's full-text search, so not a random sample.

corpora.name: ai-clin33
corpora.what: The Dutch LLM-generated test texts of the CLIN33 shared task (GPT-4 and Vicuna-13B): news 200, tweets 200, book reviews 200, poetry 50. The 100 generated opinion columns were removed in 0.2.0 because they make invented claims about real, named people. Not product copy; it shows which connectors and register words LLMs overuse in Dutch generally.
corpora.source: CLIN33 Shared Task LLM-generated test data (Pieter Fivez, Walter Daelemans, Tim Van de Cruys; University of Antwerp, KU Leuven), https://zenodo.org/records/10732813
corpora.license: CC BY 4.0, redistributed with attribution (see NOTICE).

corpora.name: ai-general
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering plain requests in six genres (blog post, email to colleagues, short essay, newspaper article, LinkedIn post, short report) on eight everyday topics, made by scripts/generate-general.mjs from scripts/general-requests.json. The models saw no pattern list. The general entries added in 0.2.0 and 0.3.0 were drawn from this set, so its hit rates overstate recall; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are the clean held-out measure.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only, 96 texts. Claude Code put the account's email address in the context, and Sonnet signed 11 emails across the three languages with the account owner's name; that name was replaced by a neutral one and the rows carry a 'redacted' note. The model ids were not recorded at generation; each row carries the id the alias resolved to with the same CLI version on the same day.

corpora.name: ai-general-holdout
corpora.what: Claude Sonnet (48) and Claude Haiku (48) answering the requests in scripts/general-requests-holdout.json: the same six genres as ai-general, eight new topics. Written after the 0.2.0 general entries were chosen. Its results were read during the 0.3.0 review rounds, so it is no longer a clean held-out estimate; ai-multi-holdout and ai-detailed-holdout are. Each row records the resolved model id and the system prompt, which tells the model to ignore the account email in its context.

corpora.name: ai-multi-holdout
corpora.what: Six models answering plain one-line requests from scripts/multi-requests.json: seven genres (blog post, email to friends, short essay, local newspaper article, Instagram post, short report, and a long article of about 800 words) on eight everyday topics that appear in no other corpus. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 56 requests each (224 texts). OpenAI GPT-5.5 (gpt-5.5-2026-04-23) answered the six short genres on the first topic (6 texts) and GPT-5.4 mini (gpt-5.4-mini-2026-03-17) the six short genres on the first four topics (24 texts). Sent through the OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages APIs by scripts/generate-api.mjs with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit: the models saw only the request and never a pattern list. Each row records the generator, provider, resolved model id, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: OpenAI is kept small for budget: 30 of 254 texts, two models, no long form, so the GPT rows show direction only. Every reply ended normally (stop or end_turn) and is at least 200 characters long. The Claude rows were checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

corpora.name: ai-detailed-holdout
corpora.what: Realistic requests with concrete facts, as people type them to a chat assistant: 56 scenarios (eight per genre, the same seven genres as ai-multi-holdout, outlined in scripts/detailed-scenarios.md), each written twice in the language, as a short request (style A, one or two sentences) and a careful one (style B, with audience, tone, length and the facts as notes), in scripts/detailed-requests/nl.json. Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5), Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5), Claude Haiku 5.5 (claude-haiku-5-5) and Claude Sonnet 4.5 (claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929) answered all 112 requests each, through the Anthropic Message Batches API (scripts/generate-api.mjs batch) with no system prompt, default sampling and a 16,000 token limit. Most scenarios are set in the Netherlands (336 texts), the rest in Flanders (112); each row carries the variety. Each row records the generator, resolved model id, style, scenario, the exact request and the stop reason. Made after the lists of this release were final, never used to choose or tune an entry, and measured once.
corpora.caveats: Anthropic models only. The requests were written for this study by a model that did not see the pattern lists, following the scenario outline; names, places, addresses and contact details in them are invented. Every reply ended with end_turn and was checked for the right language, personal data, refusals and duplicates. Email addresses, web addresses and phone numbers that could belong to a real person or business were replaced after generation with example.* addresses and placeholder numbers, in the requests and in the replies alike.

notUsed: Wayback Machine snapshots of etsy.com/nl/listing pages (2018-2022): about 100 pages fetched and parsed, none had Dutch as the original listing language (the /nl/ text is Etsy's machine translation), and the archive started refusing requests.
The Common Crawl index API for .nl product URLs timed out (HTTP 502 and 504) on 2026-10-27.
The human half of the CLIN33 data is not in the public Zenodo record.
